## What they do (the principles, not the exact tools)
1. **The game IS the hook.** Headline turns the viewer into a player: "CAN YOU SPOT THE FAKE MILLIONAIRE? 👀" / "1 Fake Millionaire 💀" / "Millionaires vs Larper 💀". Short, one line, ends on 💀/👀. Titles are tiny and vibe-y ("a walking larp 💀", "that was unexpected 🤯") + `| @fomo`.
2. **Go contestant by contestant.** Tight on one masked contestant at a time (Iron Man, Batman, the clown, the "D" mask), each making their claim, so the viewer judges each one.
3. **Illustrate every flex claim.** When a contestant names what they own: a cut-out PNG of the item (Mercedes GT63, red BMW M3, blue Mustangs, a yellow Birkin) + a small label of the item ("GT63", "M3 in Singapore", "Mustangs", "Handbag bro") + the price in **green money text with a black outline** ("$180,000+", "$80,000+", "$150,000+"). Small, at chest height, never covering faces.
4. **Captions are small and keyword-only**, coloured per word (green / yellow / cyan), placed on the speaker's chest, not big centred word-by-word.
5. **Verdict beats.** A big red glowing **"FAKE"** stamp over the line-up; a green colour-wash highlight on the one contestant being judged; confetti on the reveal.
6. Layouts: CLASH = white top bar with black + red headline, video below; Krazy = black bars, white headline with 💀.

## How to use them on OUR FOMO clips (fits the brief + earlier feedback)
- Use: the spot-the-fake game headline, contestant-by-contestant pacing, item cut-out + green price text on real flex claims (only prices that are SAID in the episode, never invented: brief bans invented net worths), coloured keyword captions.
- Careful: the user said earlier "keep the spoilers away and stop covering the video with cards". So: the item pops are small and short (≤ 1.5 s, chest height, faces clear), and the **FAKE stamp only goes on someone the panel ACCUSES in the clip, never the real answer** (Iron Man) unless the clip is the reveal itself.
